name: Qualitative or Quantitative Defects of Collagen VI

criteria.description: Presence of progressive muscle weakness and contractures predominantly affecting proximal muscles
Muscle biopsy showing reduced or absent collagen VI expression by immunohistochemistry
Identification of pathogenic variants in COL6A1, COL6A2, or COL6A3 genes
Characteristic muscle MRI showing selective muscle involvement with fatty infiltration
Presence of early-onset joint contractures and skin abnormalities such as keloids or hyperkeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus either muscle biopsy findings or pathogenic genetic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by combining clinical, histological, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Proximal muscle weakness with early contractures
searchTerms: proximal weakness with early joint stiffness
muscle loss near trunk with contractures
weakness and tight joints in limbs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent collagen VI expression in muscle tissue
searchTerms: lack of collagen VI in muscles
collagen protein deficiency in muscle tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic muscle MRI pattern with selective muscle involvement
searchTerms: distinct muscle involvement pattern on MRI
selective muscle damage seen on imaging
loose joints at fingers and toes

common.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to diaphragmatic weakness
Skin abnormalities including keloid formation and follicular hyperkeratosis
searchTerms: skin scars and thickened hair follicles
keloid scars and rough skin bumps
skin abnormalities with scarring and follicle changes

common.symptomName: Scoliosis developing during childhood or adolescence

rare.symptomName: Severe respiratory failure requiring ventilatory support
searchTerms: life-threatening breathing failure needing ventilator support

laboratory: Reduced collagen VI protein expression in muscle biopsy by immunohistochemistry
Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective fatty infiltration of the anterior thigh and posterior calf muscles
Chest imaging may show diaphragmatic elevation
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COL6A1, COL6A2, or COL6A3 genes identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Pulmonary function tests indicating restrictive lung disease

distinguishingFeatures: Bethlem myopathy typically has milder contractures and later onset
Less frequent respiratory involvement compared to collagen VI defects
More severe muscle weakness and contractures at birth
Prominent distal joint hyperlaxity and skin changes
Different genetic causes and muscle biopsy findings

redFlags: Marked reduction or absence of collagen VI on muscle biopsy
references: Merlini L, et al. Collagen VI myopathies. Neuromuscul Disord. 2008;18(4):273-82.
